title: Bad Trips Guide, Round 29
intro: Round 29 (2026-11-09). The word-for-sense read of the whole guide is done: three fresh readers, a third each, asked of every word whether it's the word meant, and the read was tested with errors I planted where they couldn't see the list. They found all nine, so what they didn't flag can be trusted too ([what each finding was, and what came of it](https://github.com/u-dont-existDOTcom/joel-articles/blob/claude/bad-trips-20261105/articles/bad-trips/humanize/h38-20261109/sense-read/RESULTS.md)).

Three slips were in the guide's drafted text, so I fixed them: the medics heading is now "Call medics for:" (the line under its list already says the remedies can begin while help is arranged), "Test them" under Stillness or Movement? now says "Test stillness and movement", and the list after "Don't take more" now goes "cannabis or ketamine, do intense breathwork, fast, ...", since breathwork and fasting aren't taken. Two are in paragraphs you wrote yourself, and they're these two cards. Three stay as they are: "often mistaken as shadow work" is your round-1 wording, "the first thread" is the poster's thread of the two you link, and a "2." that looked stray was only in my copy for the readers.

edits.before: Humic acid when eaten, can produce a hyperintelligent state for me. From the outside that may look manic, and it could destabilize somebody prone to mania or without meditation training. I wouldn't use it casually during a bad trip. Smelling it does not produce that hyper intelligent state but does feel relaxing and very beneficial for brain health, so I'd start with that.
